chunks.content: PROCUREMENT EXCEPTIONS HANDBOOK ================================ ProcureBuddy Knowledge Base Supplement - Edge Cases & Exceptions Source: Compiled from GFR 2025, CSIR Manual 2019, and SnT Special Provisions Chapter 1: PAC (Proprietary Article Certificate) Exceptions ------------------------------------------------------------ Rule 166 - Single Tender / Proprietary Purchase 1.1 When is PAC Required? A PAC certificate is mandatory when procurement is made from a single source (proprietary purchase) under Rule 166 of GFR 2025. The competent authority must certify that the item is proprietary in nature and cannot be obtained from any other source. 1.2 Who Can Issue PAC? The PAC must be issued by a competent technical authority. In CSIR laboratories, this is typically the Head of the Department or a Senior Scientist who has domain expertise to certify the proprietary nature of the item. The PAC cannot be issued by the procurement section or administrative staff alone. 1.3 Conditions for

chunks.file_name: Procurement-Exceptions-Handbook.txt
chunks.content: or a Senior Scientist who has domain expertise to certify the proprietary nature of the item. The PAC cannot be issued by the procurement section or administrative staff alone. 1.3 Conditions for Proprietary Purchase: - The item is manufactured or supplied by only one firm (sole manufacturer/sole dealer) - Standardization with existing equipment requires the same make/brand - Genuine emergency where time does not permit competitive bidding - Interchangeability requirements with existing systems 1.4 PAC Without Proprietary Justification: Single tender can also be used without PAC in cases of: - Genuine emergency (must be recorded with detailed justification) - Standardization (must be approved by competent authority with cost comparison) - After failure of OTE/LTE where re-tendering is not feasible 1.5 PAC Issued by Non-Competent Authority: If a PAC is issued by someone who does not have the technical competence or is not the designated authority, the procurement is NON-COMPLIANT. This

This is a High Audit Risk item. The purchase may be challenged by the audit party. 1.6 Retired Scientists and PAC: A retired scientist CANNOT issue a valid PAC certificate. The certificate must be issued by a serving officer of the laboratory who holds the competent authority designation at the time of issuing the certificate. 1.7 Audit Risk of PAC Procurement: PAC-based procurement carries Medium to High audit risk. Required evidence includes: - The PAC certificate itself with detailed reasons - Market survey report (if available) - Competent authority approval - Record of why competitive bidding was not feasible Chapter 2: Threshold Boundary Cases ------------------------------------- 2.1 Exact Threshold Boundaries: - Up to Rs. 50,000 (inclusive): Direct Purchase under Rule 154 - Rs. 50,001

If it is Rs. 5,00,001 or above, it moves to LTE. The boundary is determined by the estimated cost at the time of initiating procurement. 2.3 LPC Cannot Handle Above Rs. 5 Lakhs: If the estimated cost is Rs. 5,00,001 or more, the LPC route is NOT applicable. The procurement must follow the LTE route under Rule 162 with minimum 3 firms invited. 2.4 Estimated Cost vs Actual Cost: The procurement method is determined by the estimated cost at the time of initiating the process. If the lowest quotation exceeds the threshold slab, a revised cost

Chapter 3: Bid and Tender Exceptions -------------------------------------- 3.1 Fewer Than 3 Quotations in LTE: Under Rule 162, limited tender requires invitation to a minimum of 3 firms. If fewer than 3 quotations are received, the case should be referred to the purchase committee which may recommend: - Accepting available quotes with recorded justification - Re-tendering with wider invitation - Converting to OTE if market conditions warrant 3.2 Single Bid in OTE: If only one bid is received in an Open Tender, the committee should: - Examine if the tender was given adequate publicity - Check if specifications were too restrictive - Consider re-tendering with modified terms - If

This applies regardless of the procurement value. 4.2 When GeM Can Be Skipped: - Item is not available on GeM (requires GeM-not-feasible certificate) - Required specification/configuration not available on GeM - Delivery timeline on GeM cannot meet urgent requirement - Items under SnT special provisions with specific exemptions 4.3 GeM Portal Down: If GeM portal is temporarily unavailable, the buyer should: - Document the downtime with screenshots - Record the date and time of attempted access - If urgency permits,

Price alone is not a valid reason to skip GeM. 4.5 Items Below Rs. 25,000 on GeM: Even for small purchases below Rs. 25,000, if the item is available on GeM, it should preferably be procured through GeM. chunks.content: Chapter 5: Order Splitting and Clubbing ----------------------------------------- 5.1 Artificial Splitting is NOT Allowed: Splitting a procurement into multiple smaller orders to bring each order below a threshold slab is strictly prohibited. This is considered circumvention of rules and carries HIGH AUDIT RISK. Example: A purchase requirement of Rs. 30 lakhs cannot be split into two orders of Rs. 15 lakhs each to avoid OTE requirement. 5.2 Clubbing of Small Items: When multiple small items are needed for the same purpose or project, they should be assessed for: - Whether they can be clubbed into a single procurement - Whether they constitute a single procurement requirement - The aggregate value determines the procurement method If 50 different items each worth Rs. 50,000 are needed, the aggregate value (Rs. 25 lakhs) should determine the procurement route, not individual item values. 5.3 Legitimate Separate Purchases: Items can be purchased separately if they are genuinely different

However, for recurring procurement, having a panel of registered vendors improves efficiency. 8.2 Debarment of Suppliers: Suppliers can be debarred (blacklisted) for: - Supply of substandard goods - Non-compliance with contract terms - Submission of forged documents - Fraudulent practices The debarment process requires an inquiry and competent authority approval. Debarment period is typically 1-3 years depending on severity. 8.3 Foreign Vendors: Foreign vendors can

Import procurement follows the same basic GFR rules but with additional requirements for import license, customs clearance, and foreign exchange provisions. 8.4 Sole Authorized Dealer: If a vendor claims to be the sole authorized dealer for a product, verify: - Whether the OEM confirms dealership exclusivity - Whether other dealers or the OEM directly can supply - Whether genuinely no alternative sources exist Only after verification should the proprietary/single tender route be considered. Chapter 9: Committee and Authority Exceptions ----------------------------------------------- 9.1 Same Person as Indenting and Approving: The same person should NOT be both the indenting officer and the approving authority for the

chunks.content: Exceptions ----------------------------------------------- 9.1 Same Person as Indenting and Approving: The same person should NOT be both the indenting officer and the approving authority for the same procurement. Separation of duties is a fundamental audit principle. However, in small laboratories with limited staff, this may be unavoidable, and the next higher authority should be made aware. 9.2 Finance Concurrence: Finance concurrence is required for procurement above the delegated financial powers. The provisions contained in GFRs are deemed to be applicable to Autonomous Bodies except to the extent the bye-laws of an Autonomous Body provides for separate Financial Rules which have been approved by the Government. Rule 2 Definition: In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires- (i) “Accounts Officer” means the Head of an Office of Accounts or the Head of a Pay and Accounts Office set up under the scheme of departmentalization of accounts; (ii) “Administrator” means Administrator of a Union Territory, by whatever name designated; (iii) “Appropriation” means the assignment, to meet specified expenditure, of funds included in a primary unit of appropriation; (iv) “Audit Officer”

chunks.content: PRICE VARIATION CLAUSE The formula for Price Variation should ordinarily include a fixed element, a material element and a labour element. The figures representing the material element and the labour element should reflect the corresponding proportion of input costs, while the fixed element may range from 10 to 25%. That portion of the price represented by the fixed element will not be subject to variation. The portions of the price represented by the material element and labour element alone will attract Price variation. The formula for Price variation will thus be: P1 =P0 F+a - P0 Where P1 is the adjustment amount payable to the supplier (a minus figure will indicate a reduction in the Contract Price) P0 is the Contract Price at the base level. F is the Fixed element not subject to Price variation. a is the assigned percentage to the material element in the Contract price. b is the assigned percentage to the labour element in the Contract Price. L0 and L1 are the wage indices at the

chunks.file_name: UpdatedGFR31July2025_0.pdf
chunks.content: variation. a is the assigned percentage to the material element in the Contract price. b is the assigned percentage to the labour element in the Contract Price. L0 and L1 are the wage indices at the base month and year and at the month and year of calculation respectively. M0 and M1 are the material indices at the base month and year and at the month and year of calculation respectively. If more than one major item of material is involved, the material element can be broken up into two or three components such as Mx, My & Mz. Where price variation clause has to be provided for services (with insignificant inputs of materials) as for example in getting technical assistance normally paid in the form of per diem rates, the price variation formula should have only two elements viz. a high fixed element and a labour element.
